correctness.rationale: A mixed factor cannot repeat: two occurrences of an unequal-letter bigram would witness a,b,a,b. The counts of (k−1)-factors minus indegrees and outdegrees prescribe both endpoints of the order-(k−1) factor trail, including when they coincide; descending by factor counts and the prescribed suffix recovers all shorter counts from such a trail. After deleting homogeneous loops a^k, the only repeated vertices are a^{k−1} belonging to two separate runs. Each such run must have length exactly k−1, with no loops, since the multiplicity bound is 2k−2. Any deleted loops accordingly belong to vertices with just one remaining visit. Repeated vertices in the contracted source trail cannot interleave. To verify the step-5 uniqueness hinge, suppose another contracted trail first departs differently at v. The source must have two departures from v, so the rival takes the later one first. No vertex strictly between the two source visits to v occurs outside that interval, as that would interleave with v. Thus the internal vertices of the return segment have no entrance from outside except the bypassed first departure; the only unused incoming edge to v is the return from that segment. After taking the second departure first, the rival cannot get back to use the first, a contradiction. This proves uniqueness of the contracted trail, and the deleted loops restore uniquely at their sole visits. Rivals are not assumed noncrossing; shorter words are immediate from their complete spectra. The sharpness pair has precisely the same one a^k and the same k factors containing the singleton b, with matching (k−1)-suffix, hence identical complete spectra. The block containing 1 leaves j noncrossing subproblems and gives the stated generating function, while injectivity makes the whole source optimal.
